description:
Implement a flight data benchmark using the US Bureau of Transportation Statistics
(BTS) On-Time Performance dataset. This benchmark provides realistic time-series
analytics on commercial aviation data spanning decades, enabling performance
testing of temporal aggregations, route analysis, and delay pattern detection.

The BTS dataset is excellent for benchmarking because:
- Real operational data from US commercial airlines (1987-present)
- Multi-dimensional analysis: temporal, geographic, carrier, aircraft
- Predictable scale factors based on historical coverage
- Rich analytical patterns: delays, cancellations, routes, seasonal trends
- Well-documented schema with stable data quality

Use cases covered:
- On-time performance analysis
- Delay cause attribution
- Route and airport performance rankings
- Seasonal and temporal patterns
- Carrier comparisons

context_sections:
- name: Data Sources
  summary: |
    **Primary Source: BTS TranStats**
    - URL: https://www.transtats.bts.gov/ontime/
    - Format: CSV (customizable download)
    - Coverage: January 1987 - present (monthly updates)
    - Cost: Free (public data)

    **Alternative Sources:**
    | Source | Coverage | Format | Access |
    |--------|----------|--------|--------|
    | BTS TranStats | 1987-present | CSV | Direct download |
    | Kaggle | 2018-2024 | CSV/Parquet | Download |
    | AWS Open Data | Historical | Parquet | S3 access |
    | OpenSky Network | Global, real-time | JSON/Parquet | API (academic) |

    **Recommended for BenchBox:**
    - BTS TranStats for authoritative US data
    - Pre-converted Parquet for faster loading
    - Kaggle datasets for quick prototyping

- name: Schema Structure
  summary: |
    **Core Fields (simplified from full BTS schema):**

    | Field | Type | Description |
    |-------|------|-------------|
    | Year, Month, DayofMonth | INT | Date components |
    | DayOfWeek | INT | 1=Monday, 7=Sunday |
    | FlightDate | DATE | Full flight date |
    | Reporting_Airline | STRING | Carrier code |
    | Flight_Number_Reporting_Airline | INT | Flight number |
    | Origin, Dest | STRING | Airport codes |
    | CRSDepTime, CRSArrTime | INT | Scheduled times (HHMM) |
    | DepTime, ArrTime | INT | Actual times (HHMM) |
    | DepDelay, ArrDelay | FLOAT | Minutes delayed |
    | Cancelled | INT | 0/1 flag |
    | CancellationCode | STRING | A=Carrier, B=Weather, C=NAS, D=Security |
    | Diverted | INT | 0/1 flag |
    | Distance | FLOAT | Miles |

    **Delay Attribution Fields:**
    - CarrierDelay, WeatherDelay, NASDelay, SecurityDelay, LateAircraftDelay

    **Dimension Tables:**
    - Airlines (carrier code -> name mapping)
    - Airports (code -> name, city, state, coordinates)

- name: Data Volumes
  summary: |
    **Annual Flight Volumes (approximate):**
    | Period | Flights/Year | Notes |
    |--------|--------------|-------|
    | 2019 | 7.4 million | Pre-pandemic peak |
    | 2020 | 4.7 million | COVID impact |
    | 2021 | 5.4 million | Recovery |
    | 2022-2024 | 6-7 million | Near pre-pandemic |

    **Historical Totals:**
    - 1987-2024: ~200+ million flights
    - Single year: ~50-100 MB (compressed)
    - Full historical: ~5-10 GB (compressed)

- name: Query Workload Categories
  summary: |
    **On-Time Performance (5+ queries):**
    - On-time arrival rate by carrier
    - Delay distribution by airport
    - Average delay by time of day
    - Best/worst performing routes
    - Improvement trends over time

    **Delay Analysis (4+ queries):**
    - Delay cause breakdown
    - Cascading delay patterns (LateAircraftDelay)
    - Weather vs carrier-controlled delays
    - Recovery time analysis

    **Route Analytics (4+ queries):**
    - Busiest routes by flight count
    - Route reliability rankings
    - Distance vs delay correlation
    - Hub connectivity patterns

    **Temporal Patterns (4+ queries):**
    - Day-of-week patterns
    - Seasonal variations
    - Holiday impact analysis
    - Time-of-day congestion

    **Carrier Comparisons (3+ queries):**
    - Carrier ranking by on-time %
    - Cancellation rates by carrier
    - Market share by route

- name: Scale Factor Design
  summary: |
    **TPC-aligned scale factors (SF=1 ≈ 1GB raw data):**

    Full dataset: ~200M flights (1987-present), ~15-20 GB raw.
    Per flight: ~75-100 bytes. Scale factors use time-based subsetting.

    | Scale | Period | Flights | Size (Raw) | Use Case |
    |-------|--------|---------|------------|----------|
    | 0.01 | ~1 week | ~140K | ~10 MB | CI/testing |
    | 0.1 | ~2 months | ~1.2M | ~100 MB | Development |
    | 1.0 | ~1.5 years | ~10M | ~1 GB | Standard |
    | 10.0 | ~15 years | ~100M | ~10 GB | Large scale |
    | 100.0 | Full (37y) | ~200M | ~15-20 GB | Maximum |

    **Scaling Strategy:**
    - Time-based (contiguous years) for trend analysis
    - Recent years preferred for relevance
    - Maintain referential integrity with dimension tables
    - Note: Full dataset (~200M flights) is smaller than SF=100 convention

anti_patterns.dont: download real flight data in unit tests
anti_patterns.why: files are large and BTS rate-limits

anti_patterns.dont: embed full airport/airline datasets inline in code
anti_patterns.instead: use downloadable CSV files with version pinning
